messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 detected: repeated CUDA driver resets + container restarts on gpu-pool-12, error pattern matches slow paged-allocator memory creep. Auto-created incident channel #inc-6677889900 :rotating_light:
michelle: seeing elevated 5xx rate from hosted cluster, alerting oncall now. logs show oom/killed in runtime container and repeated nvml driver faults.
arjun: on it, pulling node logs. can someone check kv-cache stats for that pool?
ben: `kubectl -n runtime logs svc/serve-gpu-12 -c runtime --since=30m | grep -i oom` -> lots of `Killed process 2378 (served) total-vm:...` entries.
eva: nvml output from node: `GPU 0: Xid 31` repeated, then container restart.
michelle: customer impact: a subset of requests hitting long-context models failed (~7% p50 latency spike, 3% error increase for streaming endpoints). Not full outage but visible.
arjun: hypothesis: paged-attention allocator fragmentation + KV cache sticky pages causing slow memory drift until OOM. I've seen similar when prefix caching accumulates many small pinned pages.
ben: running quick heap stats from runtime admin endpoint: `GET /admin/heap?detail=kv_cache` -> `pinned_pages: 12403, fragmented_slots: 732, reclaimable: 4.2%`
eva: paging metrics: `pager.reclaims=1.2/min, pager.allocations=18/min, slab_frag_ratio=0.68` — that reclaim rate is too low for the allocation churn.
sre-pager: started live-triage doc: https://redwood.internal/triage/6677889900 (posted for runbook checks).
arjun: immediate mitigation plan: 1) mark node `gpu-pool-12` unschedulable, 2) drain existing jobs slowly, 3) enable aggressive eviction config on allocator `--kv-evict-threshold=0.6`, 4) restart runtime service after enabling compact-on-start.
michelle: agree. I'm doing the cordon now. `kubectl cordon gpu-pool-12` -> done.
ben: draining with `kubectl drain gpu-pool-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300` starting. will watch job handoffs.
eva: while drain runs, flip live-config for allocator: `redwoodctl config set runtime.pagedAllocator.evictAggressiveness=high --env=prod` then restart on one node to test.
arjun: doing a rolling restart on a single replica first. command: ```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-serve -n runtime --selector=pool=gpu-12
```
ben: restarted one runtime pod, observing logs. After restart, `pinned_pages` dropped to ~3200 on that pod and slab_frag_ratio -> 0.32. Good signal.
michelle: customer ops notified EMEA customers impacted, advising retries and short backoff. no major escalations yet.
sre-pager: adding followups: collect `dmesg` and `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` for last 24h, and nvml samples `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` for next 30m.
arjun: still seeing occasional Xid 31 from same GPU when under heavy prefix load. Might be hitting driver bug under fragmentation + long KV reuse. Opening ticket to upstream driver with stack dump.`
ben: I'm scheduling a compact job across the rest of the pool: `redwoodctl runtime compact --pool gpu-12 --mode=fast` (will run after drain completes).
eva: after compaction, eviction config will revert to default in 2 hours if stable. setting an auto rollback in config service.
michelle: oncall handoff at 08:00 UTC tomorrow to @arjun-night. Leaving notes in ops doc with commands and current mitigations. :white_check_mark:
arjun: filing incident summary: memory drift from KV/paged allocator caused progressive fragmentation and driver faults. mitigation: cordon & drain, aggressive eviction, restart runtime pods with compact-on-start, run pool-wide fast compaction. next steps: reproduce in staging with long prefix workload and increase compaction cadence.
sre-pager: updated incident channel with runbook checklist and assigned follow-ups: driver ticket, allocator tunables review, longer-term: auto-compact heuristics per pool.
ben: will follow up with perf team to tune `evictAggressiveness` default for long-context routes.
michelle: thanks team. I'll hand off any incoming alerts to arjun during night. leaving final status: partial customer impact, mitigated by compaction + restarts, watch for regressions. :pray:
